title: The merge tool tells a replacement PR from a new one, so a guard change's replacement PR keeps its review rounds owed
why: The merge tool cannot tell a replacement PR from a new one, so a guard-yes record reads done after a round 1 PASS while the lane still owes rounds 2 and 3 (lane fail-record-ancestor-head, recorded on PR 1957, 06:45 CST Nov 8). Replacement PRs are common (#1911 replaced #1907; #1371 replaced #1326).
note: Fix: a PR body line naming the PR it replaces carries the old PR's rounds into the new record, and a guard-yes record after a round 1 PASS on a replacement reads not done until rounds 2 and 3 land; red case first. Queue fix (owner 13:20 CST Nov 7). Filed 06:47 CST Nov 8; the coordinator assigns a lane. Doing in lane fail-record-ancestor-head (session_013NEJKzYhDtNPLcEdeVFEVe) as a follow-up to PR 1957 (coordinator, 06:28 CST Nov 8). Open scope question with the coordinator: every guard-yes record, or replacement PRs only. Scope read by triage 06:51 CST Nov 8: past rulings answer it, so no page question. Item 359 b (owner, Nov 7 14:41 CST): skip round 3 unless the change touches a guard or check, or round 2 failed. Item 402 a: a guard or check change gets round 3 and the net-value test even after an earlier fix check passes. Neither is scoped to replacement PRs, so every guard-yes record owes round 3 (the lane's option a). The open PRs 1881, 1892 and 1951 owe their round 3 under those rulings. Covered by #1773 (the merge tool refuses a guard lane without round 3; rounds 1-3 PASS at e19ae8874); the coordinator stopped the second check (06:30 CST Nov 8). Done when #1773 merges.
